definitions: A design pattern in software development, particularly within reactive programming frameworks, that combines the concepts of signals (for reactive state management) and a centralized store (for managing application state) to provide a predictable and efficient way to manage and react to changes in application data.

A architectural approach often seen in front-end frameworks that leverages reactive signals to update components when data in a central store changes, promoting unidirectional data flow and improved performance.
examples: Implementing the Signal Store Pattern improved state management.
The Signal Store Pattern simplifies data flow.
Consider the Signal Store Pattern for your next project.
